newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA MAKE SOUND START VS S.AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA MAKE SOUND START VS S.AFRICA.

text.p: Australia made a sound start on the first morning of the third and final cricket test match against South Africa at Centurion Park on Friday.
South Africa's gamble on inserting the tourists after winning the toss failed to pay significant dividends as Australia reached 64 for the loss of just two wickets by lunch.
Mark Waugh was not out at the interval but more significantly Australian skipper Mark Taylor survived the session in his personal battle for batting form.
Despite leading his side to nine successive wins in South Africa and a winning 2-0 lead in the test series, there had been calls for Taylor to be dropped as a result of his poor batting performance.
However he reached an undefeated 22 by lunch to end a run of nine test innings in which he failed to reach 20.
South Africa were looking to restore some pride after losing tests in Johannesburg and Port Elizabeth, but skipper Hansie Cronje's decision to bowl first on a well grassed wicket did not pay off.
They had success in the eighth over when recalled left arm fast bowler Brett Schultz bowled Matthew Hayden through the gate for ten.

It took an injudicious hook at an Allan Donald bouncer from Matthew Elliott to get the second breakthrough. Schultz took a fine running catch over his right shoulder just a couple of metres in from the fine leg boundary to dismiss Elliott for 18.
Schultz replaced the injured Shaun Pollock with South Africa also dropping batsman Herschelle Gibbs and wrist spinner Paul Adams in favour of all-rounder Lance Klusener and off-spinner Pat Symcox.
